description_en: No reliable information could be garnered regarding the building's history and its date of construction. However, it is very similar in size and style to a mansion in Phaplu that was built in the first decade of the 20th century. The owner, an elder Sherpa gentleman, lives in Kathmandu and has not been in Junbesi for many years. According to local informants the owner's children have little interest in maintaining the estate. The owner's sister (Sherpa, 67 years old) lives with her family in New York City since 1999. She occasionally visits Junbesi and has little recollection of her upbringing in the mansion. She married young and established a new household with her husband on the west side of Junbesi. For the past 25 years different caretakers have been staying in the house and at some point a teacher from the Junbesi primary school rented a room on the first floor. The house is currently uninhabited.
description_ne: यो घर कहिले र कसले बनायो भन्ने कुराको ऐतिहासिक जानकारी केहि पनि उपलब्ध छैन । घरको मालिक एक जना स्थानीय शेर्पा हुन् तर उनी वर्षौँदेखि काठमाण्डुमा बस्ने गर्दछन् । घर मालिककी अमेरिका को न्युयोर्क् शहरमा बसोबास गरिरहेकी ६७ वर्षीय छोरीले भने अनुसार तल्लो पुस्ताहरू भने यो घरको रेखदेख गर्न थोरै उत्साहित छन् । उनीभने बिरलै मात्र जुनबेँसी जाने गर्दछिन् । विगत २५ वर्षदेखि यता यो घरमा रेखदेख गर्न राखेका मानिसहरू मात्रै बस्ने गर्दथे । कुनै समयमा जुनबेँसी प्राथमिक विद्यालयमा पढाउने शिक्षक पनि यस घरमा डेरा गरी बसेका थिए । अहिले यो घर खाली छ ।
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired), Repaired
